pr_title: Feat: Allow setting security_and_analysis settings in gh repo edit
pr_body:
Fixes #10091

I took a stab at implementing changes to `security_and_analysis` properties in [gh repo edit](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_edit). My Go is a bit rusty, but I did my best to match the project's style. Would love any feedback on how to make this better!

A few notes:
* `security_and_analysis` properties don't seem to be available in the [GraphQL API](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/objects#repository) which is used by interactive mode in `gh repo edit`. For that reason, I didn't include the ability to change these properties in interactive mode for now.

* `--enable-secret-scanning-push-protection` cannot be enabled unless `--enable-secret-scanning` is enabled, but the API doesn't throw an error for this, the UI will simply not reflect the change. I didn't add a check for this in `gh repo edit` for now.

* From this comment on the issue:
> TBD: Need to determine what an informative error looks like based on the response from the API, and whether we can do anything valuable.

If a user doesn't have admin permissions:
`HTTP 404: Not Found (https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>)`

If features are not supported:
`HTTP 422: Secret scanning is not available for this repository.(https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>)
`

issue_context.title: Allow setting security_and_analysis settings in gh repo edit
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

[`gh repo edit`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_edit) allows setting most properties of [`octokit.rest.repos.update`](https://octokit.github.io/rest.js/v21/#repos-update). But, it doesn't seem to have an option for `security_and_analysis` properties that I can find.

From the docs and the OpenAPI types, that's:

* `advanced_security`
* `secret_scanning`
* `secret_scanning_push_protection`

### Proposed solution

Could we be able to set those properties in `gh repo edit` too, please? I.e.:

```shell
gh repo edit --enable-advanced-security true --enable-secret-scanning true --enable-secret-scanning-push-protection true
```

### Additional context

Is there precedent for what does or doesn't get implemented in `gh repo edit`? And if so, is that influenced at all by which settings are within nested objects like `security_and_analysis`?

Sibling issue to: #10092
comments:
> Is there precedent for what does or doesn't get implemented in `gh repo edit`? And if so, is that influenced at all by which settings are within nested objects like `security_and_analysis`?

@JoshuaKGoldberg : For perspective, the GitHub CLI is maintained separately from the GitHub teams who manage repositories, issues, pull requests, actions, etc there is a bit of disconnect with what is implemented within REST or GraphQL API and whether it makes its way to all of the various client apps.  So it falls our small group of maintainers to manage the breadth of capabilities.

This seems reasonable to me. There's no particular precedent, as Andy says, it's really just a matter of coordination and someone asking for it.

The three flags you ask for seem to be present in [GHES 3.13](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.13/rest/repos/repos?apiVersion=2022-11-28), so there's no backwards compatibility concerns, though a more recent one `secret_scanning_validity_checks` is not yet in GHES apparently.

Based on the docs, it seems like there are extra permissions required to view and to set these fields, so we'll need to make sure that we correctly handle that.

> In order to see the security_and_analysis block for a repository you must have admin permissions for the repository or be an owner or security manager for the organization that owns the repository. For more information, see "[Managing security managers in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/managing-security-managers-in-your-organization)."

### Acceptance Criteria

This A/C is focused on the mutation aspect of these flags. We may want to surface these via `gh repo view` and `gh repo list`, particularly in the `--json` format, but that can be a separate issue.

#### Advanced Security

**Given** I have the necessary permissions
**And Given** I have a repo that has advanced security off
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-advanced-security true`
**Then** I see in the Web UI that advanced security has been configured on

**Given** I have the necessary permissions
**And Given** I have a repo that has advanced security on
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-advanced-security false`
**Then** I see in the Web UI that advanced security has been configured off

**Given** I do not have the necessary permissions
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-advanced-security true/false`
**Then** I see an informative error

#### Secret Scanning

**Given** I have the necessary permissions
**And Given** I have a repo that has secret scanning off
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning true`
**Then** I see in the Web UI that secret scanning has been configured on

**Given** I have the necessary permissions
**And Given** I have a repo that has advanced security on
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning false`
**Then** I see in the Web UI that secret scanning has been configured off

**Given** I do not have the necessary permissions
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning true/false`
**Then** I see an informative error

#### Secret Scanning Push Protection

**Given** I have the necessary permissions
**And Given** I have a repo that has secret scanning push protection off
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning-push-protection true`
**Then** I see in the Web UI that secret scanning push protection has been configured on

**Given** I have the necessary permissions
**And Given** I have a repo that has advanced security on
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning-push-protection false`
**Then** I see in the Web UI that secret scanning push protection has been configured off

**Given** I do not have the necessary permissions
**When** I run `gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning true/false`
**Then** I see an informative error

TBD: Need to determine what an informative error looks like based on the response from the API, and whether we can do anything valuable.

Tangent: I'm really impressed with the depth of response (acceptance criteria! past context!) _and_ with how fast you responded with it. Thank you very much, this was awesome to see!

If I still remembered any of my Go I would absolutely contribute here. 🥲
I'd like to take on the implementation of this issue if it's still available :)
Sure thing, give it a go.

review_comments:
This test doesn't give me confidence that the code is behaving as expected. Setting the `SecurityAndAnalysis` struct on `opts` manually here is short-circuiting the flag handling, meaning there's no coverage in the logic that transforms the bool flag to the API struct.

That said, I don't expect this test to change with the refactor I've suggested around the transformation logic (turning the bool flag into the API struct). I would expect to see a few tests covering that function, though, which should shore up the gap in our testing, here 🙂

Added unit tests for the transformer function:
* enable all 
* disable all
* enable only one
* disable only one

Do you think these provide enough coverage?

~~Yup! And the new set of tests are great! Thanks~~ 🙌 

This is definitely enough coverage for the transformer, but I think I realized we're missing one more test covering the failed permissions check that I discovered after writing this comment. I've explained it in [this comment](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/10139#discussion_r1898615505).
